title: Inequalities
lede: Solving for a range of answers instead of one, and the one rule that trips everyone up.

sections.md:
## Reading inequality signs
| Sign | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| < | less than | x < 5 |
| > | greater than | x > −2 |
| ≤ | less than or equal to | x ≤ 10 |
| ≥ | greater than or equal to | x ≥ 0 |

The open side of the sign faces the bigger number. "At least" means ≥. "At most" and "no more than" mean ≤.

## Solving
Solve exactly like an equation, with **one exception**:

**When you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, flip the sign.**

Why? 2 < 5 is true. Multiply both by −1: −2 and −5. Now −2 is the **bigger** one, so the sign must flip: −2 > −5.

## Graphing on a number line
Use an **open circle** for < or > (the endpoint isn't included) and a **closed circle** for ≤ or ≥ (it is). Shade the direction of the solutions.
